claims.text: The as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy has a fine lamellar microstructure of alternating soft FCC and hard B2 phases.
A fine alternating lamellar architecture promotes preferential localized degradation at phase boundaries during simultaneous high-temperature wear and corrosion.
Wear preferentially removes protective oxide films at lamellar interfaces.
The FCC and B2 phases have different electrochemical potentials.
Exposed FCC and B2 phases form localized galvanic couples.
Localized galvanic coupling accelerates corrosion.
Galvanic corrosion also accelerates mechanical material removal.
Elevated temperature accelerates diffusion and oxidation under the proposed conditions.
Lamellar phase boundaries are sites of enhanced electrochemical activity.
Lamellar phase boundaries are susceptible to enhanced mechanical disruption.
Corrosion weakens the phase boundaries.
Corrosion-weakened phase boundaries increase wear-particle generation and microstructural delamination.
Oxide removal, galvanic corrosion, boundary weakening, and particle generation form a self-reinforcing degradation cycle.
Combined wear and corrosion produce significantly greater total degradation than isolated wear or isolated corrosion.
Damage under combined exposure is preferentially localized at lamellar phase boundaries.
Combined exposure increases the corrosion rate relative to the isolated-exposure baselines.
Combined exposure increases wear-particle generation relative to the isolated-exposure baselines.
Protective oxide films remain more intact during isolated wear or isolated corrosion, producing lower degradation rates.
The mechanism applies when wear removes oxide locally without completely homogenizing the surface.
Quantitative wear-corrosion relationships may vary with phase distribution and experimental conditions.

contradictions.description: The proposed immersion in an aqueous 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution at 700°C is physically incompatible with ordinary liquid immersion unless a sufficiently pressurized vessel is specified; alternatively, a molten-salt or vapor environment would be required.

The mechanism states that wear removes protective oxide, whereas the predicted outcome groups isolated wear with isolated corrosion as conditions in which oxide films remain more intact. Isolated sliding wear could itself remove oxide, so this comparison requires qualification.
